question.text: The variation of the velocity of a particle with time is represented in the given v–t graph. Between t = 0 and t = 40 s, the graph forms two identical triangular lobes: it starts from rest at t = 0, increases linearly to a maximum of 5 m/s, returns linearly to 0 at t = 20 s, then drops linearly to a minimum of −5 m/s before increasing linearly back to 0 at t = 40 s. Determine:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: The total distance covered by the particle in the first 40 s.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: The average velocity of the particle throughout this 40 s duration.

conditions: peak positive velocity is 5 m/s between t = 0 and t = 20 s
minimum negative velocity is −5 m/s between t = 20 s and t = 40 s
velocity returns to 0 at t = 40 s

figure.description: A velocity-time (v–t) graph with velocity v on the vertical axis and time t in seconds on the horizontal axis. A triangular wave starts at the origin (0, 0), rises to a peak velocity of 5 m/s, and descends linearly to touch the time axis at t = 20 s. From t = 20 s, it continues downward linearly to a trough of −5 m/s, and then rises linearly to meet the time axis again at t = 40 s.

solution.approach: The area under a velocity-time graph gives distance and net displacement, so split the graph into its two triangular parts and combine them.

steps.text: The graph forms two triangles: velocity is positive from 0 to 20 s, reaching a peak of 5 m/s, and negative from 20 to 40 s, reaching a minimum of −5 m/s.
steps.equation: base = 20 s, height = 5 m/s for each triangle

steps.text: Find the area of the first triangle, the distance covered while the velocity is positive.
Find the area of the second triangle, the distance covered while the velocity is negative.
Total distance travelled is the sum of the magnitudes of both areas.
Net displacement is the signed sum: the positive area cancels the negative area, so the particle returns to its starting position.
steps.why_this_step: Displacement uses the sign of each area, not just its size, while distance adds the sizes.

steps.text: Average velocity is the net displacement divided by the total time; state both results.
steps.equation: Average velocity = 0 m / 40 s = 0 m/s; Distance = 100 m, Average velocity = 0 m/s

common_mistakes.text: Taking the net area (50 m − 50 m = 0) as the distance travelled gives 0 m instead of the correct 100 m.
Using only the first triangle's area as the total distance gives 50 m instead of 100 m.
